chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn Zaydawayh al-Jalab al-Hamdani in Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Amroos al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn al-Hukam, from his father, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salma, from Abu Sa'd al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whomever Allah has bestowed with the love of the Imams from my Household has attained the good of this world and the Hereafter. Let no one doubt that he is in Paradise, for in the love of my Household there are twenty characteristics: ten of them are in this world and ten of them are in the Hereafter. As for those in this world: asceticism, eagerness for action, piety in religion, desire for worship, repentance before death, energy in night prayer, despair of what is in people's hands, preserving Allah's commands and prohibitions, the ninth is dislike of the world, and the tenth is generosity. As for those in the Hereafter: his record will not be spread out, no scale will be set up for him, his book will be given to his right hand, freedom from the Fire will be written for him, his face will be whitened, he will be clothed in the garments of Paradise, he will intercede for one hundred members of his family, Allah will look upon him with mercy, he will be crowned with one of the crowns of Paradise, and the tenth is that he enters Paradise without reckoning. Blessed be those who love my Household.

key_terms.الزُّهْدُ: Asceticism or detachment from worldly desires
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: The Imams, specifically from the Prophet's Household
key_terms.الْمِيزَانُ: The scale of deeds on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْوَرَعُ: Piety and God-consciousness in religious matters
key_terms.بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ: Without reckoning or detailed accounting of deeds
key_terms.قِيَامُ اللَّيْلِ: Night prayer or standing in prayer at night

ai.seo_question: What are the twenty characteristics of loving the Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a cornerstone of Shia theology, emphasizing that love for the Ahl al-Bayt is not merely emotional but a transformative force yielding tangible spiritual and eschatological benefits. The narration categorizes these twenty virtues into worldly ethical disciplines—such as asceticism and vigilance—and otherworldly honors like being presented with one's record by the right hand and interceding for one's family, reflecting the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Prophet's Household.
